examined_formations.title: MONTHLY_WORDPRESS_CARE_AND_MAINTENANCE_PLAN
examined_formations.chinese_title: WordPress 月度维护与托管照护
examined_formations.evidence_summary: WP Buffs currently sells direct monthly WordPress care plans from $89 to $359 per site and a white-label program that maintains thousands of sites with recurring monthly invoicing. The repeatable layer—backup, update, uptime and security monitoring—is already heavily automatable through current WordPress tooling such as WP Umbrella; the remaining value in the managed plan is engineers handling edits, emergencies, compatibility failures and custom-site exceptions. The buyer spend is real and recurring, but the exact productized-service category already exists and its differentiated residual remains recurring human technical support.

examined_formations.title: MONTHLY_DEDICATED_GENERAL_VIRTUAL_ASSISTANT_SUBSCRIPTION
examined_formations.chinese_title: 通用虚拟助理月度订阅
examined_formations.evidence_summary: Wing currently sells general virtual-assistant capacity at $699/month for 80 hours and $999/month for 160 hours, including a dedicated assistant, customer-success management and quality control. This is strong direct non-role purchase evidence, but the purchased unit is explicitly dedicated human time and contextual execution. Productization removes hiring friction; it does not create founder-independent machine delivery or a distinct compounding operator asset.

examined_formations.title: UNLIMITED_GRAPHIC_AND_PRESENTATION_DESIGN_SUBSCRIPTION
examined_formations.chinese_title: 不限量平面与演示设计订阅
examined_formations.evidence_summary: ManyPixels currently sells flat monthly design subscriptions at $699, $1,199 and $1,399 with unlimited requests/revisions, project management and designer assignment. Canva's current Magic Design can already generate on-brand designs and presentation drafts from prompts. The market therefore has both mature human design subscriptions and native AI for the repeatable draft layer; the residual willingness to pay concentrates in taste, brand interpretation, revision judgment and creative quality control.

examined_formations.title: PODCAST_AUDIO_POSTPRODUCTION_PER_EPISODE_AND_MONTHLY_PLAN
examined_formations.chinese_title: 播客音频后期按集与月度托管
examined_formations.evidence_summary: We Edit Podcasts currently sells audio postproduction from $180, $320 and $550+ per episode and supports month-to-month plans without long-term contracts. Descript now automates transcription, filler-word and retake removal, Studio Sound, chaptering, show notes and social clips through its AI co-editor. The repeatable editing layer is increasingly self-serve/native; the residual premium scope is advanced narration, storytelling, content strategy, show-specific taste and final editorial judgment.

examined_formations.title: MANAGED_QA_AS_A_SERVICE_MONTHLY_OUTCOME_SUBSCRIPTION
examined_formations.chinese_title: 托管式 QA-as-a-Service 月度结果订阅
examined_formations.evidence_summary: BetterQA currently sells subscription QA from €1,400/month per engineer with tools and outcome tracking, while QA Wolf sells an end-to-end managed QA outcome that combines specialized AI agents with dedicated engineers and guarantees 80%+ E2E coverage. The desired outcome is already an exact mature managed-service category. Automation owns an increasing share of mapping, generation, execution and maintenance, while product-specific test strategy, exploratory testing and domain judgment remain human.

examined_formations.title: ON_DEMAND_CAD_DRAFTING_AND_ENGINEERING_DESIGN_PURCHASE
examined_formations.chinese_title: 按项目购买 CAD 制图与工程设计
examined_formations.evidence_summary: Cad Crowd currently sells vetted CAD/design outcomes through flat-rate quotes and prepaid hourly blocks and reports more than 33,000 designs delivered and 1,500+ satisfied clients. Autodesk Fusion already automates 2D drawing generation and adds AI/automation across design workflows, including generative design. The remaining high-value scope is geometry interpretation, manufacturability, code/discipline constraints, engineering review and liability—expert work rather than a normalized machine-executable operator unit.
